after.name: after
after.description: Wraps a function so it only runs starting from its `count`-th call.

ArrayElement.name: ArrayElement
ArrayElement.description: Extracts the element type of an array or tuple.

bfs.name: bfs
bfs.description: Breadth-first traversal of a graph given as an adjacency list.

binarySearch.name: binarySearch
binarySearch.description: Finds the index of a value in an array sorted ascending, in O(log n); returns `-1` if absent.

Brand.name: Brand
Brand.description: Tags a primitive type so structurally-identical values from different domains can't be mixed up (nominal typing).

chunk.name: chunk
chunk.description: Splits an array into chunks of the given size.

clamp.name: clamp
clamp.description: Restricts a number to the given inclusive range.

compact.name: compact
compact.description: Removes every falsy value (`false`, `0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, `NaN`) from an array.

compose.name: compose
compose.description: Composes functions right to left: the last one runs first, fed with the original arguments.
examples:
const shout = compose((s: string) => s + "!", (s: string) => s.toUpperCase());
shout("hi"); // "HI!"

constant.name: constant
constant.description: Creates a function that always returns the given value.

countBy.name: countBy
countBy.description: Counts array items grouped by the given selector.

debounce.name: debounce
debounce.description: Wraps a function so it only runs after `delay` ms of silence.
examples:
const onResize = debounce(() => console.log("resized"), 200);
window.addEventListener("resize", onResize);

deepMerge.name: deepMerge
deepMerge.description: Recursively merges plain objects, later sources winning on conflicts; arrays and non-plain values are replaced outright, not merged element-wise. Never mutates its inputs.

DeepMutable.name: DeepMutable

DeepPartial.name: DeepPartial
DeepPartial.description: Recursively makes every property of `T` (including nested

DeepReadonly.name: DeepReadonly
DeepReadonly.description: Recursively makes every property of `T` (including nested

DeepRequired.name: DeepRequired
DeepRequired.description: Recursively makes every property of `T` (including nested

defaults.name: defaults
defaults.description: Fills in `undefined` properties of an object from one or more source objects, without mutating any of them.

dfs.name: dfs
dfs.description: Depth-first traversal of a graph given as an adjacency list.

difference.name: difference
difference.description: Returns the values in an array that are not present in any of the other arrays.

DistributiveOmit.name: DistributiveOmit
DistributiveOmit.description: Like `Omit`, but distributes over a union instead of collapsing it first. Plain `Omit` on a discriminated union only sees the keys common to every member, so it silently drops the union's other fields; this keeps them.

Entries.name: Entries
Entries.description: A typed version of `Object.entries`'s return shape: an array of `[key, value]` tuples for `T`.
examples:
type UserEntries = Entries<{ id: string; age: number }>;
// Array<["id", string] | ["age", number]>

escape.name: escape
escape.description: Escapes `& < > " ' \`` so a string is safe to drop into HTML.

EventEmitter.name: EventEmitter

fibonacci.name: fibonacci
fibonacci.description: Returns the n-th Fibonacci number (0-indexed: `fibonacci(0) === 0`, `fibonacci(1) === 1`), memoized across calls.

first.name: first
first.description: Returns the first element of an array, or the first `n` when given.

flattenObject.name: flattenObject
flattenObject.description: Flattens a nested object into a single level, joining keys with `.` (e.g. `{ a: { b: 1 } }` becomes `{ "a.b": 1 }`). Arrays are kept as leaf values, not descended into.

gcd.name: gcd
gcd.description: The greatest common divisor of two integers (Euclidean algorithm).

get.name: get
get.description: Safely reads a nested property by a dot/bracket path (e.g. `"a.b[0].c"`), returning a fallback if any step is missing.

groupBy.name: groupBy
groupBy.description: Groups array items into a record keyed by the given selector.

identity.name: identity
identity.description: Returns its single argument unchanged. Useful as a default/no-op callback.

initial.name: initial
initial.description: Returns every element except the last `n` (default 1).

intersection.name: intersection
intersection.description: Returns the values common to every passed array.

invert.name: invert
invert.description: Swaps an object's keys and values.

isEmpty.name: isEmpty
isEmpty.description: Checks whether a value has no content: `null`/`undefined`, an empty array/string, an empty `Map`/`Set`, or an object with no own keys.

isEqual.name: isEqual
isEqual.description: Deep-compares two values: arrays, dates, and plain objects are compared by content.

isPrime.name: isPrime
isPrime.description: Checks whether an integer is prime, by trial division up to `sqrt(n)`.

JsonValue.name: JsonValue
JsonValue.description: Any value that survives a `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse` round-trip: a primitive, or nested arrays/objects of those.
examples: const config: JsonValue = { a: 1, b: [true, null, "x"] };

last.name: last
last.description: Returns the last element of an array, or the last `n` when given.

lcm.name: lcm
lcm.description: The least common multiple of two integers.

levenshteinDistance.name: levenshteinDistance
levenshteinDistance.description: The minimum number of single-character edits (insert, delete, substitute) to turn one string into another.

LinkedList.name: LinkedList
LinkedList.description: A singly linked list — O(1) push/shift, O(n) random access.

LiteralUnion.name: LiteralUnion
LiteralUnion.description: A union of literal values that still accepts any value of the base type — keeps editor autocomplete for the literals without losing flexibility (unlike `T | string`, which collapses to just `string`).
examples:
type Size = LiteralUnion<"sm" | "md" | "lg", string>;
// autocompletes "sm" | "md" | "lg", but still accepts any other string

LRUCache.name: LRUCache
LRUCache.description: A fixed-capacity cache that evicts the least-recently-used entry once full — O(1) `get`/`set`.

memoize.name: memoize
memoize.description: Caches a function's results, keyed by its first argument (or a custom resolver).
examples:
const square = memoize((n: number) => n * n);
square(4); // 16

Merge.name: Merge
Merge.description: Shallowly merges two object types; `U`'s properties override `T`'s on conflict — the type-level version of `{ ...t, ...u }`.

mergeSort.name: mergeSort
mergeSort.description: Sorts an array with merge sort — stable, guaranteed O(n log n). Returns a new array, does not mutate the input.

Mutable.name: Mutable
Mutable.description: Strips `readonly` from every top-level property of `T`.

negate.name: negate
negate.description: Wraps a predicate so it returns the opposite boolean.
examples:
const isOdd = negate((n: number) => n % 2 === 0);
isOdd(3); // true

noop.name: noop
noop.description: Does nothing and returns `undefined`. A placeholder default callback.

Nullable.name: Nullable
Nullable.description: Allows `T` or `null` — distinct from an optional property, which also allows `undefined`.
examples:
type MaybeUser = Nullable<{ id: string }>;
// { id: string } | null

omit.name: omit
omit.description: Builds a new object without the given keys.

once.name: once
once.description: Wraps a function so it only ever runs the first time it's called.

partial.name: partial
partial.description: Pre-fills a function's leading arguments, returning a function for the rest.
examples:
const greet = (greeting: string, name: string) => `${greeting}, ${name}!`;
partial(greet, "Hello")("world"); // "Hello, world!"

PartialBy.name: PartialBy
PartialBy.description: Makes the given keys of `T` optional while leaving the rest

PartialRecord.name: PartialRecord
PartialRecord.description: A `Record` where every value is optional — shorthand for `Partial<Record<K, V>>`.
examples:
type Flags = PartialRecord<"dev" | "prod", boolean>;
// { dev?: boolean; prod?: boolean }

partition.name: partition
partition.description: Splits an array into two: items that pass the predicate, and items that don't.

pick.name: pick
pick.description: Builds a new object containing only the given keys.

pipe.name: pipe
pipe.description: Composes functions left to right: the first one runs first, each result feeding the next. The mirror image of `compose`.
examples:
const shout = pipe((s: string) => s.toUpperCase(), (s: string) => s + "!");
shout("hi"); // "HI!"

pluck.name: pluck
pluck.description: Extracts a single property's value from every item in an array.

Prettify.name: Prettify
Prettify.description: Flattens an intersection type into a single object type, so
examples:
type Merged = Prettify<{ a: string } & { b: number }>;
// hovers as { a: string; b: number }

PriorityQueue.name: PriorityQueue
PriorityQueue.description: A binary min-heap: `pop()` always returns the item with the lowest priority number first.

pull.name: pull
pull.description: Removes every occurrence of the given values from an array.

Queue.name: Queue

quickSort.name: quickSort
quickSort.description: Sorts an array with quicksort (Lomuto partition, average O(n log n)); returns a new array, does not mutate the input.

random.name: random
random.description: Returns a random integer, inclusive of both bounds. With one argument, the range starts at 0.

range.name: range
range.description: Builds an array of numbers from `start` up to (excluding) `stop`, by `step`.

RequireAtLeastOne.name: RequireAtLeastOne
RequireAtLeastOne.description: Keeps every key of `T` optional, except that at least one of the given `K` keys must be present.

RequiredBy.name: RequiredBy
RequiredBy.description: Makes the given keys of `T` required while leaving the rest

rest.name: rest
rest.description: Returns every element except the first `n` (default 1).

retry.name: retry
retry.description: Retries an async function up to `attempts` times, waiting with exponential backoff between tries. Rethrows the last error once attempts run out.

sample.name: sample
sample.description: Picks one random element from an array, or `n` distinct random elements.

set.name: set
set.description: Writes a nested property by a dot/bracket path (e.g. `"a.b[0].c"`), creating intermediate objects as needed. Mutates and returns `obj`.

shuffle.name: shuffle
shuffle.description: Returns a new array with the same elements in random order (Fisher-Yates).

sleep.name: sleep
sleep.description: Returns a promise that resolves after the given delay.

Stack.name: Stack
Stack.description: A LIFO stack — push/pop/peek in O(1).

StateMachine.name: StateMachine
StateMachine.description: A minimal finite state machine: define allowed transitions per state, then `send()` events and read `.state`.

throttle.name: throttle
throttle.description: Wraps a function so it runs at most once per `wait` ms — immediately on the leading call, then once more on the trailing edge if calls kept coming in.
examples:
const onScroll = throttle(() => console.log("scrolled"), 200);
window.addEventListener("scroll", onScroll);

times.name: times
times.description: Invokes a function `n` times, collecting the results.

Trie.name: Trie
Trie.description: A prefix tree for fast word/prefix lookup — the classic structure behind autocomplete.

unescape.name: unescape
unescape.description: Reverses {@link escape}: turns HTML entities back into their literal characters.

unflattenObject.name: unflattenObject
unflattenObject.description: Rebuilds a nested object from dot-notation keys — the inverse of `flattenObject`.

union.name: union
union.description: Merges arrays and removes duplicates, keeping first-seen order.

UnionToIntersection.name: UnionToIntersection
UnionToIntersection.description: Converts a union type into an intersection of its members.
examples:
type Combined = UnionToIntersection<{ a: string } | { b: number }>;
// { a: string } & { b: number }

uniq.name: uniq
uniq.description: Removes duplicate values from an array, optionally by a derived key.

uniqueId.name: uniqueId
uniqueId.description: Generates a unique string id, optionally with a prefix. Backed by a per-process counter.

ValueOf.name: ValueOf
ValueOf.description: The union of every value type in `T` — like `keyof T`, but for values.

XOR.name: XOR
XOR.description: Exclusive-or of two object types: allows the shape of `T` or the shape of `U`, but never a mix of both.

zip.name: zip
zip.description: Transposes a list of arrays: groups every array's i-th element together.

zipObject.name: zipObject
zipObject.description: Builds an object from parallel key/value arrays, or from `[key, value]` pairs.
